lengthsNote: Metres, typical adult. ankleHeight: floor→ankle joint. footFront / heel: ball of the foot in front of / heel behind the ankle. midfoot: balance point in front of the ankle. trunk: hip→shoulder joint. hipHalfWidth / shoulderHalfWidth: midline→hip / shoulder joint. chestDepth: height of the bar on the chest above the shoulder joints, lying on a bench.
trunkPartsNote: For the holding muscles (lower and upper back): head and trunk split as in de Leva's table (fraction of body mass; together = headTrunk). Placed along the hip → shoulder line: head 0.13 m above the shoulders, upper trunk halfway between mid-back and shoulders, middle trunk 70% of the way from L5/S1 to mid-back (positions estimated). l5s1: the lumbosacral joint, metres above the hip joints along the trunk (estimate, TODO: source).

grip.note: Men's median peak grip (ages 29–39, best of both hands, crush grip on a dynamometer). Holding a bar isn't a crush grip (the hand wraps a fixed handle), so this is a rough capacity.
grip.source: Dodds RM, Syddall HE, Cooper R, Benzeval M, Deary IJ, Dennison EM, et al. (2014). Grip strength across the life course: normative data from twelve British studies. PLoS ONE 9(12):e113637. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0113637 (49,964 participants; women's peak median 31 kg)

holdingStrengthNote: Rough capacities for the holding (isometric) loads, so they can show an effort: men's values, scaled by the strength slider (an entry {nm} for a torque, {kgPerHand} for the grip). The lower back has none on purpose: Graves et al.'s isolated lumbar extension (237 N·m with the spine neutral) put a 100 kg deadlift at 155%, far below what trained lifters hold. The upper back, neck and shoulder blades have no usable norm yet (Garcés et al. 2002's neck values are given in N in the text but labelled N·m in the tables).
massNote: mass: fraction of body mass per segment (one leg or arm; the masses sum to 1 for the whole body). com: centre of mass as a fraction of segment length, measured from the ankle (shank), knee (thigh), hip (head + trunk), shoulder (upper arm) or elbow (forearm + hand, along elbow → grip). From de Leva's table for young adult males; head + trunk is the mass-weighted combination (head centre of mass placed about 0.13 m above the trunk's top), which lands at 66% of hip → shoulder.
source: de Leva P (1996). Adjustments to Zatsiorsky-Seluyanov's segment inertia parameters. J Biomech 29(9):1223–1230. doi:10.1016/0021-9290(95)00178-6 (Table 4, males)
